source_text: Invisibilis et incomposita terra erat, antequam Deus diceret: Fiat lux, et antequam divideret inter lucem et tenebras. Tenebrae erant super abyssum — illam nimirum in qua erit diabolus et angeli eius. Propterea Deus solvit tenebras: Fiat lux, et facta est lux. Et vocavit Deus lucem diem et tenebras noctem. Et factum est vespere et factum est mane, dies una — non dixit dies prima, quia tempus nondum erat ante mundum.
pass_a_gloss: Invisible and unordered earth was, before God said: Let-be light, and before he-divided between light and darknesses. Darknesses were over abyss — that namely in which will-be devil and angels his. Therefore God loosed darknesses: Let-be light, and made is light. And called God light day and darknesses night. And made is evening and made is morning, day one — not he-said day first, because time not-yet was before world.
pass_b_english: The earth was invisible and unordered before God said [[Let there be light >> Bible:Genesis 1:3]] and before he divided light from darkness. Darkness was over the abyss — that abyss in which the devil and his angels will be. So God dissolves the darkness: Let there be light, and light was made. He called the light Day and the darkness Night. [[There was evening and there was morning, day one >> Bible:Genesis 1:5]] — he did not say “first day,” because time was not yet before the world.
